$comment: OWNER-OWNED FILE. This manifest is the single source of truth for which gates exist and what each one runs. An executing agent may ADD a gate, but may never remove a gate, change a locked command string, rename a gate id, or turn a blocking gate non-blocking. gates.manifest.lock is the freeze record of {id, command, blocking} and scripts/check-gate-manifest.mjs enforces the difference. The gate set may only grow. If a gate will not pass, the correct response is to report BLOCKED with the real command output — never to edit this file.

gates.name: gate manifest integrity
gates.proves: The frozen gate set has not shrunk, had a locked command changed, or stopped blocking.

gates.name: plan closed-world lint
gates.proves: Every plan file is closed-world by the nine rules in .planning/PLAN-STANDARD.md.

gates.name: commit discipline audit
gates.proves: No commit since project init mixes apps/inheritance/ with paths outside it.

gates.name: engine tests
gates.proves: The Rust succession engine's 442 unit, integration, and fuzz-invariant tests pass.

gates.name: wasm build
gates.proves: The engine compiles to WebAssembly and lands a real binary in frontend/src/wasm/pkg/. The script verifies existence, a 100 KB size floor, and the 0061736d WebAssembly magic number — wasm-pack exiting 0 is not accepted as proof on its own.

gates.name: frontend suite vs ledger
gates.proves: The complete, unmodified 2,416-test Vitest suite runs and its failure set exactly equals the known-failure ledger.

gates.name: typecheck
gates.proves: Zero TypeScript errors. --force is required, not optional: tsconfig.tsbuildinfo was historically committed, and an incremental run can no-op against a stale cache and report clean on a tree that has type errors.

gates.name: gate skip accounting
gates.proves: Every gate reports how many of its own assertions it skipped, and every skip is declared in the shrink-only gate-skips.lock ledger.

gates.name: published gate results
gates.proves: gate-results.json describes the current run, covers every manifest gate, and never reports a status outside pass, fail, cannot-run and not-run.

gates.name: lawyer decision registry
gates.proves: Every recorded interpretive choice exists in both the agenda and the registry, still resolves to the rule it governs, and cannot have its status advanced without a recorded answer.

gates.name: engine observability
gates.proves: The engine still emits warnings, the legitime and free-portion split, and a structured boundary error. All ten spec-defined manual review flag codes are declared and exercised, and neither hardcoded line that suppressed observability has returned.

gates.name: engine coverage report
gates.proves: A per-module coverage report is producible for every engine module, no module has vanished from it, and the set of modules no test enters at all has not grown. See GATES.md section 10.

gates.name: assertion discipline
gates.proves: No frontend test asserts nothing, and no test whose only matcher is toBeDefined or toBeTruthy exists outside the shrink-only assertion-baseline.json ledger. See GATES.md section 11.

gates.name: journey harness self-test
gates.proves: The journey harness still works: a rubric returns structured per-assertion output and rejects an unknown kind, a perceptual diff separates a reference miss from a size mismatch from a pixel failure, a failing step writes five durable artifacts naming both failing mechanisms, and the database-free seeding seams reach a page before first paint. See GATES.md section 12.

gates.name: journey registry integrity
gates.proves: Every declared journey step has a rubric built from the closed eight-kind assertion set and an approved reference with a tolerance sidecar, and no reference exists without a step. Static: needs no Docker, no Supabase, no build and no browser. See GATES.md section 13.

gates.name: tenant isolation
gates.proves: Against a real local Supabase, a user in org A reads zero of org B's cases, PDFs and share tokens, changes zero of org B's rows, and is refused a cross-tenant insert — each paired with a positive control on the same table so a denial cannot be mistaken for an empty table. See GATES.md section 13.

gates.name: live journey run
gates.proves: Every declared account, organization and case-intake screen is driven in a real headless browser against the built application and a real local Supabase, and each is checked twice — a fixed list of yes/no DOM assertions and a zero-tolerance perceptual diff against an approved reference. See GATES.md section 13.

gates.name: money parity
gates.proves: Every peso figure the results view displays is equal, as an exact integer number of centavos, to a distribution the compiled engine computed during the same run — and the result the product stored in the database equals it too. No expected figure is committed anywhere. See GATES.md section 14.

gates.name: share exposure
gates.proves: The product's one anonymous data path returns exactly the six columns migration 015 enumerates and none of nine forbidden ones, a disabled share returns zero rows, and an unknown token returns zero rows — all through the anon key. See GATES.md section 14.

gates.name: seo smoke
gates.proves: All fourteen public landing, blog and marketing routes load in a real browser, each rendering a non-empty h1, logging no console error, and fetching nothing that answers HTTP 400 or above. See GATES.md section 14.

gates.name: pdf toolchain
gates.proves: A PDF's text, page count, page dimensions and page images are all readable by the harness, a generated document extracts its money token as one uninterrupted string with no corrupted glyph, and rasterising the same document twice produces identical images. Needs no Docker, no Supabase, no browser and no build. See GATES.md section 15.

gates.name: pdf structure
gates.proves: The PDF the product's own export button produced contains every section it renders, every amount it prints equals as an exact integer number of centavos an amount the compiled engine produced in the same run, no amount appears that the engine did not produce, and every heir with a share has a named narrative and a matching article citation. No expected figure is committed anywhere. See GATES.md section 15.

gates.name: pdf visual
gates.proves: Every page of the produced PDF is compared pixel for pixel against an approved reference at a tolerance of zero, and a page appearing or disappearing fails on page count before any pixel is compared. The gate has no write path into the reference directory. See GATES.md section 15.

gates.name: print layout
gates.proves: The print stylesheet's effect is read from what the browser computed and printed: the print typeface and body size from computed style under print media, navigation and no-print elements proven hidden and print-only elements proven shown, the page size read as A4 out of the browser's own printed document, and the margins measured as the distance from the paper edge to the first ink. The check opens no stylesheet. See GATES.md section 15.

gates.name: blocked requirements
gates.proves: The three lawyer-blocked requirements LAW-06, LAW-07 and LAW-12 are recorded against the decision each waits on, the record agrees with .planning/lawyer-decisions.json, none of them is marked complete while its decision is still awaiting-answer, and an arriving answer raises ANSWER ARRIVED and fails the build rather than passing silently. See GATES.md section 16.

gates.name: spec legal text
gates.proves: The four passages of law named in .planning/research/LEGAL-CONFORMANCE.md section 2b read correctly, checked as literal strings at named anchors in named files, with the superseded wording proven absent. See GATES.md section 17.

gates.name: legal traceability
gates.proves: Every Civil Code article cited by the engine's production code is either mapped to exactly one named test function carrying its LEGAL-VECTOR marker or declared in the shrink-only engine/legal-traceability.lock, with implemented_in recomputed from source on every run so a hand-edited registry fails rather than passes. See GATES.md section 18.

gates.name: bugs ledger
gates.proves: engine/BUGS.md keeps its fixed entry shape, every open entry keeps a runnable reproduction, every closed entry keeps a stated reason, and every legal claim stays attributed to .planning/research/LEGAL-CONFORMANCE.md. The behavioural half lives in engine/tests/bugs_ledger.rs under gate G1. See GATES.md section 19.

gates.name: claude invariants
gates.proves: CLAUDE.md states six invariants covering commit scope, gate immutability, halting, money units, single-source-of-truth and what requires a lawyer; every cited command is a live gate command in gates.manifest.json; the section sits outside every <!-- GSD:*-start/end --> generated block so a regeneration cannot silently delete it. See GATES.md section 20.

gates.name: new rule procedure
gates.proves: .planning/NEW-LEGAL-RULE.md documents article, vector, failing run, one-site implementation and registration in five ordered steps, names every artifact each step needs, and its worked example still resolves to a real article in engine/legal-rules.json, a real engine file and a real test function carrying that article's // LEGAL-VECTOR: marker. See GATES.md section 21.

gates.name: doc claims
gates.proves: Eleven documentation claims are re-probed from the tree on every run rather than compared against a frozen expectation, so a stale claim in CLAUDE.md or .planning/codebase/*.md fails and a code regression surfaces as PROBE FLIPPED; every surviving contradiction is declared in the shrink-only .planning/DOC-DEBT.md, which is held in both directions. See GATES.md section 22.

gates.name: planning truth
gates.proves: The ROADMAP Progress table, .planning/STATE.md's counters, .planning/ORIENTATION.md's pointers and RESUME.md's gate count all agree with the filesystem and the frozen manifest; phase status is derived by counting *-PLAN.md against *-SUMMARY.md and never judged. Red-on-drift by design. See GATES.md section 23.
